name: Camera mast
whatItIs: A mast at the front of the deck. Pancam and the navigation cameras sit on top of it, about 1.4 metres above the base of the wheels.
howItWorks: Pancam's two cameras work together to take detailed, multi-wavelength, 3-D panoramic pictures from about human eye height. The mast also works as a periscope for Mini-TES, a heat spectrometer that sits inside the body and reads the heat given off by minerals in rocks and soils.

quote.text: To take panoramic color images of the Martian surface, the sun, and the sky.

found.evt-landing: Pancam and the navigation cameras look out from the top of the mast. Mini-TES, inside the body, looks out through it too.
found.evt-victoria: Pancam took the first views from the rim of Victoria crater. The layers in the crater wall were what made the place exciting.
found.evt-last-contact: The last picture was taken with the left Pancam camera through a solar filter. It came out almost black because dust had blocked the Sun.

name: Robotic arm and its tools
whatItIs: The instrument deployment device: a long hinged arm on the lower front of the body. Four tools ride on the turret at its end.
howItWorks: The arm reaches out and places one tool right up to a rock or soil for close-up study. The Rock Abrasion Tool can first grind away dust and weathered rock, so the other tools see fresh rock.

quote.text: Attached to the lower front of the WEB is the instrument deployment device, a long hinged arm which protrudes in front of the rover.

tools.name: Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT)
tools.job: Grinds away dust and weathered rock to expose fresh rock underneath.

tools.name: Alpha Particle X-Ray Spectrometer (APXS)
tools.job: Reads which chemical elements a rock or soil contains, from the way it responds to X-rays and alpha particles.

tools.name: Mössbauer spectrometer (MB)
tools.job: Identifies iron-bearing minerals, which tell about early conditions on Mars.

tools.name: Microscopic Imager (MI)
tools.job: Takes extreme close-up, black-and-white pictures of rocks and soils.

found.evt-wet-meridiani: APXS found very high levels of sulfur, in sulfate salts. The Mössbauer spectrometer found jarosite, which may point to an acidic lake or acidic hot springs.
found.evt-esperance: The tools worked one after the other. First the RAT ground into the rock; then APXS read its elements. More aluminium and silica, less calcium and iron: a sign of clay minerals.

name: Wheels and suspension
whatItIs: Six wheels on a rocker-bogie suspension.
howItWorks: Each wheel has its own motor, and the two front and two rear wheels can steer on their own. The rover is built to withstand a tilt of 45 degrees without falling over, but it is programmed to avoid tilts of more than 30 degrees.

quote.text: The wheels are attached to a rocker-bogie suspension system.

found.evt-purgatory: The wheels sank more than 10 centimetres, to the depth of the wheel hubs, in a sand ripple. Getting out took more than five weeks of planning, testing and carefully monitored driving.

name: Solar arrays
whatItIs: Solar arrays attached to the two front sides of the deck, spread out like a pair of swept-back wings.
howItWorks: They make up to 140 watts in full sunshine. The energy is stored in two rechargeable batteries.

quote.text: Power is provided by the solar arrays, generating up to 140 W of power under full Sun conditions.

found.evt-last-contact: In June 2018 a dust storm that covered the planet blanketed the rover's location and blocked the sunlight. The rover could not recharge, and it went silent.

name: Warm electronics box
whatItIs: The box-like body, called the warm electronics box (WEB). It holds the computer, the batteries and other electronics. Mini-TES is mostly inside it too.
howItWorks: It protects the electronics and keeps their temperature under control, using gold paint, aerogel insulation, heaters, thermostats and radiators.

quote.text: The warm electronics box houses the computer, batteries, and other electronic components.

name: Deck and antennas
whatItIs: The flat equipment deck on top of the body. It carries the camera mast, the antennas, a magnet array that collects airborne dust and a camera calibration target shaped like a sundial.
howItWorks: Radio contact with Earth went through a dish-shaped high-gain antenna and a low-gain antenna that does not need to be pointed. A separate UHF radio talked to spacecraft orbiting Mars.

quote.text: Pancam calibration target was in the shape of a sundial mounted on the rover deck.
